about.title: About Me
content: Hello, world! I am currently a Director - Software Engineer Lead, in Morgan Stanley finance capital reporting.
Regulatory reports such as Standardized Approach for Counterparty Credit Risk (SA-CCR),
Comprehensive Capital Analysis and Review (CCAR), Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP)
were the main regulatory reports that I worked on and / or created. My expertise involves to parallelize, scale,
and optimize these big data batch jobs to within minutes of delivery time while using minimum resource consumption.

about.title: Area of Interest
content: My outside of work interest is open source library for performant data pipeline.
High throughput, low latency, and low resource consumption are optimization skills that I like to explore.

description: Directed design and delivery of SA-CCR Scenario Analysis Service (Spring Boot, Airflow, Spark, Snowflake), enabling What-If analysis on 21 million trades (40GB) with results delivered in 11 minutes.
Established multi-java Gradle monorepo platform, standardizing build/deploy pipelines across the capital fleet and accelerating onboarding of new Java applications.
Optimized capital fleet Python Airflow platform build pipeline, for each build, reduced build time by 1 hour and 2.4GB of disk usage, default to reusing a Python virtual environment (venv).

Developed capital fleet Snowflake Runway (Liquibase) platform build pipeline testing, standardized automated testing of internal tool Runway and parallelized execution to scale in a multi-team monorepo.
Led adoption of Copilot instructions for SA-CCR Scenario Analysis service, applying code standard to code generation and code review.
Delivered SA-CCR reporting engine (Scala, Spark, DB2), aggregating 21 million trades to risk-weighted assets.

Led CCAR/ICAAP SA-CCR forecasting using Spark in-memory compute and Scala Futures on Databricks, orchestrated with Airflow and backed by Snowflake; 13-quarter forecasts (13 times the data) now finish in 10 minutes (previously 2.5 hours).

Main contributor of legacy SA-CCR Scenario Analysis service, a Python Django web service that orchestrates What-If analysis for SA-CCR. DB2 changes are integrated into the existing Scala Spark DataFrame execution plan when run with the feature flag. Enabled business to provide tactical regulatory report and accelerated business analysis of optimizing existing SA-CCR logic.
Owned legacy SA-CCR What-If service (Python, Django, DB2, Spark), enabling tactical reporting and rapid scenario testing.
Invented a Spark-based rule engine for SA-CCR that condensed hundreds of lines of policy logic into single-line configurations, simplifying maintenance and accelerating regulatory updates.

A contributor of Operational Risk reporting (Elm, AutoSys, Spring Boot, Snowflake). Owned development of forecasting capability for Operational Risk calculator and incubated downstream Axiom reporting pattern using internal Scala tool Honeycomb.

Initially contributed to user investment risk tolerance, a simple middle layer that forwards users to a third party questionnaire and collects the risk tolerance. Supported UI forward through an Angular application, and maintained session and tolerance metric through Java service.

Contributed to user profile storage, the foundational user profile DynamoDB data service (Java, AWS) to support CRUD operations of user profile. A Java service that is capable to automatically scale EC2 instances to support up to 1.5 million calls per minute with 99.999% uptime, average 500 milliseconds response time.
Led the design and implementation of user profile accounts management. A sub-service of user profile service, extending granular update pattern for user profile accounts.
Migrated over 4000 input validation tests to a separate POJO repository. Reduced Bamboo build time by over 50% from 40 minutes to less than 20 minutes.

Utilized JMeter, JProfiler, and Java AWS SDK Metric to perform level 1 and level 2 performance tests to the web services. Identified bottlenecks and tuned configurations such as CPU, RAM, task count, and client configuration. Eliminated all client timeouts and increased success rate by two 9's.
Pioneered department's first archival pipeline (Lambda, Firehose, S3), establishing a model for long-term data retention.

Designed and implemented an abstract DynamoDB access layer for common usage patterns of DynamoDBMapper. Enabled the web service to scale multiple DynamoDB tables and items without implementing a class for each.
Designed and implemented data proxy from the main service to the new service for data migration. Involved implementations of a custom client, request conversion, and error response conversion.
Teacher Assistant - Mainly to help grade assignments and exams.
Created a Java client that validates input, builds requests, and makes asynchronous calls to an internal notification service.
For integration, created a script that translates notification templates from Velocity format to Freemarker format for template migration.
Migrated settings and policies of notification generation to the internal notification service.
Grader - A graduate teacher assistant and grader for CSE114, an introductory Java class. Programmed a Python program,
lazy-ta-grade-transfer, to simplify grade transfer between csv / xls files.
Teacher Assistant - An undergraduate lab teacher assistant for CSE114, an introductory Java class.
Helped student review through practice and Q&As. Created a demo for students to get started on their project Scrimish.

technology_worked_with.name: PostgreSQL
description: I used it for my second assignment in CSE532, Principles of Database Systems.
PostgreSQL has significantly more features than MySQL, I learned some new data types, type casting, rounding, and functions.
For the assignment, I worked on creating, populating, and querying an object relational database by using the object-oriented
features of SQL1999. I created types and array columns to keep the database object relational. I also wrote recursive queries,
they are the best new things I have learned in SQL.

proud_projects.title: Datalog JSON
content: A demo for representing Datalog program in JSON. I have used it to represent predicates in D3.js graph for my school project.
Spring REST service is deployed to Google App Engine, throttling is applied to the service with 1 request per second.
Static React page is host by Github Pages, making sure not to serve static files with App Engine.
Antlr4 is used to generate the parser that helps convert the Datalog program.
Very interesting demo that utilized many different technologies.

proud_projects.title: Pacman
content: The first assignment in my class CSE537, Artificial Intelligence, that is created by UC Berkeley. For the 7th question,
I came up with a heuristic that only expand under 400 nodes by calculating the real distances between foods and the real distances
between current position to foods. However, I don't think that solution would be useful for real life, so my other solution is
very cheap to compute using manhattan distances between foods and manhattan distances between current position to foods. It
expanded less than 7700 nodes and for n foods of a game state, the complexity was O(n*n). Due to license, I can't give
link to my solution, but I am willing to share some thoughts in my developing blog section.

proud_projects.title: Byte Hunter
content: This project used Thymleaf Spring MVC for server, Vue for front-end, and Phaser for game to create a game platform.
The application is deployed on a cloud platform name Google App Engine. I started my work at the database, but eventually
end up working on one of the Phaser games name Treasure Hunter. Although the game is not fun, that is very obvious to me,
I think the code is beautiful because the game used the same Javascript to generate each level. Each level has a JSON
file to represent its configuration and map.

proud_projects.title: Seawolf
content: This project uses the Python framework TPG to create a parser for executing a script language named Seawolf.
It first uses regular expression to syntatically identify tokens in the code. Then it uses context free grammar to
evaluate the tokens semantically. When everything is alright without error or exception, the parser will trigger
the function evaluate that will recursively evaluate or execute the code. Although the project used a high level
language Python to parse a high level language, I learned a lot about the steps in creating a new programming language.

proud_projects.title: Starcraft II Cat N' Mouse Red Sea
content: I had been a Starcraft II fan since its beta launch. I worked with Starcraft I map editors before and I thought Starcraft
II's Galaxy Editor should be easy to learn. It surprised me how complex the editor is to designers. Luckily, I am also a
programmer. I found Galaxy Editor's script language very similar to C, it is a subset of C in terms of feature.
The editor was very buggy and it lacks documentation, but I figured out how to take advantage of the editor's data
structure. All data were stored in XML, all changes are just additional XML that overwrite like CSS. I simply used the
editor to figure out the XML way to change something, then I populate my mod in XML text. It was a fun experience to
mod the game. I hope you can check it out by searching the map in Starcraft II Arcade.

proud_projects.title: Journey Through Europe
content: This is the greatest JavaFX 2D transition game I ever created in class CSE219. It is a electronic version of the
board game. It used binary file to store user data and XML file to store game data. Additional to the board game,
this game has AIs that will use Dijkstra Algorithm to reach all the destinations. The best part of the project was
I wrote a program to parse a text that represents the edges between cities to XML text for the game data. It generated
more than 10,000 lines of XML! I recommend you to check it out.
